proposed.explanation:
COMI (CIB) earned far more than EFID (Edita) in 2025. COMI's net profit was 82,258,815,000 EGP (printed as 82,258,815 in EGP thousands), while EFID's was 2,695,301,670 EGP. COMI out-earned EFID by 79,563,513,330 EGP, roughly 30 times more. Year-over-year, COMI grew about 49% (from 55,256,732,000 EGP in 2024) and EFID grew about 68% (from 1,606,727,698 EGP in 2024), so EFID's growth rate was faster, but COMI's absolute profit is an order of magnitude larger.

Given your stated goal of picking the more profitable company, COMI is the clear choice on the evidence provided. I recommend buying 117 shares at 128 EGP each (14,976 EGP), leaving 15,024 EGP in cash. This keeps the single holding at roughly 50% of your 30,000 EGP portfolio, respecting the diversification cap.

Important caveats: the evidence covers only one year of net profit. I have no data on revenue, market capitalisation, share count, balance-sheet strength, dividend policy, or sector risk. A 5-year investment decision ideally rests on a much richer dataset. COMI's stock at 128 EGP is also a larger per-share commitment than EFID at 20.40 EGP, which affects liquidity if you need to exit quickly. With medium loss tolerance, you should be aware that concentrating in one stock (even at 50%) carries meaningful single-name risk. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
